description: Add a claim to a project's register, or change one — its kind, label, number in the paper, title, statement or bases. A claim is named by 'id', or by 'project' and 'label': one that does not exist yet is created (with 'statement'; 'status' says how far it is proved from the start, 'open' if left out, and 'reason' on what ground). An existing claim's status is NOT changed here — use set_claim_status, so the journal says why. A field left out keeps its value; 'bases' given replaces the whole list. Write the statement in Markdown with $…$ formulas. The label is the paper's \label: a letter, then letters, digits and ':', '.', '_', '-' — once per project, case aside; 'newLabel' renames it. Members of the project who may write only.

bases.description: What it rests on, as a JSON array replacing the list: [{"kind":"page","page":477,"note":"§3"},{"kind":"computation","ref":"kimmy/gap/m74r5u"},{"kind":"lean","ref":"D5.rank_five"},{"kind":"source","ref":"Gupta 1990, Thm 2"}]. A page is one you may open, by its id; a computation by the name a [comp:…] cites — a runner's job, or a page's saved cell 'wl:477/…/2'.

id.description: The claim to change, as list_claims returned it. Or name it by 'project' and 'label'.

kind.description: theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture or question. A new claim is a theorem unless said.

newLabel.description: A new label for an existing claim.

number.description: Its number in the paper, e.g. '5.8'; empty to clear.

reason.description: For a new claim with a status: on what ground.

status.description: For a NEW claim: how far it is proved — open, paper, computer, lean, refuted, retracted. Default open.

title.description: A short name, e.g. 'Rank 5 is decided'; empty to clear.

name: set_claim
